subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve parallel distinct ACP child-session launches and fix the ACPX/Claude launch-readiness race, or intentionally serialize/throttle rapid distinct ACPX launches?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally allow different ACP session keys to run in parallel, so changing that behavior is a product and compatibility choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve parallel launches
options.body: Run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn reproduction and fix the launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

options.title: Serialize rapid ACPX launches
options.body: Intentionally gate rapid distinct ACPX child launches, then update tests and docs to make the reduced concurrency contract explicit.

options.title: Wait for fresh reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue open with needs-info until a current ACPX/Claude reproduction proves whether the old symptom still occurs.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallel launches
recommendation.body: Run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn reproduction and fix the launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and ACPX embedding/startup work make this the best available owner for the launch-readiness versus concurrency tradeoff.
